provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: My name and my class
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state their full name.
The pupils should be able to identify their class and teacher's name.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about ourselves.
We will say our names and our class.

Content:
Each child stands up and says their full name.
The teacher helps shy children.
We then say our class name and teacher's name.
Example: "My name is Aisha. I am in Nursery 1. My teacher is Mrs. Ada."

Class activity:
Children form a circle.
Each child says their name and claps once.
The whole class repeats the name after them.

Evaluation questions:
What is your full name?
Which class are you in?
Who is your teacher?

Summary:
We can all say our names and our class.

topics.title: Greeting people
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to greet in the morning and evening.
The pupils should be able to greet elders properly.

Introduction:
We greet people every day.
Good manners start with greeting.

Content:
Morning greeting: "Good morning!"
Evening greeting: "Good evening!"
To elders we add "ma" or "sir".
Example: "Good morning ma!"
The teacher shows how to bow slightly to elders.

Class activity:
Children practice greeting the teacher.
They line up and greet morning and evening.
We use play money to pretend buying things in the market.

Evaluation questions:
How do we greet in the morning?
What do we say to an elder?
Show how to greet properly.

Summary:
We greet everyone with a smile and kind words.

topics.title: My body belongs to me
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to point to their body parts.
The pupils should be able to explain that their body is private.

Introduction:
Our body is special to us.
We must learn to take care of it.

Content:
We point to our head, shoulders, knees and toes.
We sing the head shoulders knees and toes song.
Our private parts are covered by our clothes.
No one should touch them without permission.

Class activity:
Children stand and point to body parts as named.
We play a game where children say "no" if someone tries to touch their private parts.

Evaluation questions:
Point to your eyes.
Which parts are private?
What do we say if someone touches us wrongly?

Summary:
We love and protect our own bodies.

topics.title: My family
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name people in their family.
The pupils should be able to draw their family members.

Introduction:
Family is very important.
We all have people who love us.

Content:
Family members include father, mother, sister, brother.
Some have grandparents, uncles and aunties.
We can draw our family on paper.
We use different colors for clothes.

Class activity:
Children draw their family members on paper.
They take turns to show their drawing and name the people.

Evaluation questions:
Name three people in your family.
Who lives with you at home?
Draw your mother.

Summary:
Our family loves us and we love them too.

topics.title: Sharing with friends
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to share crayons with a partner.
The pupils should be able to say please and thank you.

Introduction:
Sharing makes friends happy.
We must be kind to others.

Content:
When sharing crayons, give some to your friend.
Always say "please" when asking for something.
Say "thank you" when you receive something.
Example: "Please can I have a red crayon? Thank you!"

Class activity:
Children work in pairs to share crayons.
They draw a house together using shared materials.

Evaluation questions:
What do we say when we ask for something?
What do we say after receiving something?
Show how to share with a friend.

Summary:
Sharing and saying please and thank you makes us good friends.

topics.title: Saying sorry
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what to do when we hurt a friend.
The pupils should be able to say sorry and make up.

Introduction:
Sometimes we hurt our friends by mistake.
We must learn to say sorry.

Content:
If we hurt a friend, we say "I'm sorry".
We can also say "forgive me".
After saying sorry, we can make up by sharing a toy.
Example: "I'm sorry I took your pencil. Here is your eraser."

Class activity:
Children role play hurting a friend and saying sorry.
They practice saying sorry with a hug or handshake.

Evaluation questions:
What do we say when we hurt a friend?
How do we show we are sorry?
What does make up mean?

Summary:
Saying sorry helps fix friendships.

topics.title: Classroom rules
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to listen to class rules.
The pupils should be able to walk instead of running in class.

Introduction:
Classroom rules help us learn safely.
We all follow the rules together.

Content:
Rule 1: We listen when the teacher is talking.
Rule 2: We walk in the classroom, no running.
Rule 3: We raise our hands to speak.
Rule 4: We keep our classroom clean.

Class activity:
Children practice walking around the classroom.
When the teacher says "freeze", they stop moving.

Evaluation questions:
What is rule number 2?
Show how to walk in class.
Why do we have classroom rules?

Summary:
Following rules keeps our class safe and happy.

topics.title: Taking turns
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to wait for their turn on the slide.
The pupils should be able to take turns with toys.

Introduction:
Taking turns means sharing time.
Everyone gets a chance to play.

Content:
When playing on the slide, we wait in line.
Each child has one turn before going back to the end of the line.
With toys, we say "your turn now, my turn next".
We do not grab toys from others.

Class activity:
Children line up to use the slide one by one.
They practice saying "my turn" and "your turn" with a ball.

Evaluation questions:
What do we do before going on the slide?
What do we say when sharing a toy?
Show how to take turns.

Summary:
Taking turns is fair to everyone.

topics.title: Keeping the class clean
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to put waste in the bin.
The pupils should be able to arrange chairs after play.

Introduction:
A clean class helps us learn well.
We all help keep our class tidy.

Content:
When we have paper or trash, we put it in the bin.
After playing, we put chairs in rows.
We do not draw on walls or tables.
We wipe our desks if they are dirty.

Class activity:
Children practice throwing paper balls into the bin.
They arrange toy chairs after playing with them.

Evaluation questions:
Where do we put our waste?
What do we do after playing with chairs?
Why is it important to keep our class clean?

Summary:
We all help keep our class clean and tidy.

topics.title: Revision and role play
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to act greeting, sharing and sorry.
The pupils should be able to say class rules.

Introduction:
Today we practice what we learned.
We will play and learn together.

Content:
We review greeting by saying good morning to each other.
We practice sharing toys and saying please and thank you.
We act saying sorry when we hurt a friend.
We say our class rules together.

Class activity:
Children take turns to role play different social habits.
Some children greet, others share, others say sorry.

Evaluation questions:
Show how to greet properly.
What do we say when sharing?
What is rule number one?

Summary:
We remember to be kind and follow our rules.
